title: In, on, at for time
goal: Choose in, on or at for times, days and years
intro: A simple picture helps: “at” for exact points (at 5 pm, at night), “on” for days and dates (on Monday, on 15 August), and “in” for longer periods (in May, in 2020, in the morning). Some words take no preposition at all: this, next, last, every, tomorrow, yesterday.

rules.rule: at + clock time, night, the weekend (British), festivals as a period.
in + months, years, seasons, parts of the day.
examples: in the morning, in the evening

rules.rule: No preposition with this, next, last, every, today, tomorrow, yesterday.

mistakes.why: No preposition before next / last / this.

mistakes.wrong: I will call you in the night.
mistakes.right: I will call you at night.

ex.q: I'll see you on next Friday.
My flight is at Monday morning.
ex.fixed: My flight is on Monday morning.
ex.y: A specific day: on Monday morning.

ex.a: I get up at six in the morning.
ex.y: at + clock time, in the morning

ex.q: Correct this: “I was born on 1998 in May.”

talk: Tell the coach about important dates in your life: when you were born, when you started work or college, and your plans for next month.
